newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Airbus says outsells Boeing in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says outsells Boeing in U.S.

text.p: Airbus, the European aerospace consortium, is outperforming U.S. rival planemaker Boeing Co on its domestic market, Jonathan Schofield, Airbus chief for North America said on Tuesday.
"It's an arrogant statement but I believe we're outselling Boeing this year in North America," said Schofield, chairman and chief executive of Airbus Industrie of North America.
He told a meeting of the European Aviation Club on air travel deregulation that Airbus was not facing too many structural problems in North America.
"No one has given us a barrier to entry," he said.
"I feel quite well accepted and as long as we're selling at the rate we're selling at in North America, I consider the company extremely successful," he said.
Schofield was not worried by an agreement earlier this month between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas Corp MD to collaborate on future Boeing wide-body commercial airplane programmes.
"I think it takes two people to cause competition and think it is necessary in our business to have two," he said.
"Therefore in my mind we'll continue to compete as we did yesterday. What is going to happen to Douglas and to what extent Boeing or anyone else deals with Douglas is unknown at this point," he said.
